speaker: narrator
text: The library door was behind you now. Nib’s courier bag swung gently against his scarf. Its strap wore the soft pad from your first delivery adventure. Inside, three invitations rested in three separate pockets. Reed Hut, the Mill, and Fern Lodge were still waiting for their letters.

speaker: nib
text: A dependable bag,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib declared proudly. He inspected the doorway tag once more, although the doorway was already far away.

speaker: lark
text: And a whole woodland ahead,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark replied brightly. She opened the route book on a flat stone. Its first direction named the fork beneath the ferns. You followed a dry path, with the bag between your friends.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib’s steps grew brisk. He was eager to make the first delivery. Lark paused beside a familiar little word on the first journal page.

speaker: lark
text: Before our new clue, here is a word we already know,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark invited gently.

speaker: lark
text: Read am. Slide its two sounds if you want to.

speaker: narrator
text: At the fork stood two wooden posts. One held a carved fish, with a splendid fin rising from its back. The other carried a small wooden fan. Four broad blades turned whenever the breeze slipped between the trees.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib watched the fan turn. He took a step toward its path.

speaker: nib
text: Very lively directions,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib remarked approvingly.

speaker: nib
text: That one must be important.

speaker: lark
text: It is moving,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark observed thoughtfully.

speaker: lark
text: But movement doesn’t tell us which path the book names.

speaker: narrator
text: She rested the open book on the stone. Both little labels began with the same new letter: f. Lark showed its tall curved line and its short line across.

speaker: lark
text: Listen to the start of fan,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark invited softly.

speaker: lark
text: Touch your top teeth to your lower lip. Let the air flow gently. No hum, and no extra little vowel. Listen to our sound, then find its letter.

speaker: narrator
text: Lark set f beside the a and n you knew. She joined the sounds into fan. Then she changed just the middle letter. The little i from pin made fin.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib looked from one label to the other. The beginnings matched. So did the endings. Only the small middle was different.

speaker: nib
text: I nearly followed the biggest moving thing,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib admitted sheepishly.

speaker: lark
text: We can read the whole word,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark reminded him warmly.

speaker: lark
text: Our book names fin. Read both labels, and choose fin for our route.

speaker: narrator
text: The little i settled the question. Lark pointed to the fish’s fin. Its path curved around the fern bank, away from the fan’s short viewing alcove. The crew stayed on dry ground. No one needed to cross the creek here.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib gave the fan a courteous bow before leaving.

speaker: nib
text: Excellent spinning,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib told it sincerely.

speaker: nib
text: Different destination.

speaker: narrator
text: At a low resting stone, Lark opened your courier journal. She drew the fish post and left space beneath it for the new letter.

speaker: lark
text: We can keep our f beside today’s clue,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark suggested gently.

speaker: lark
text: Curve over, go down, then add the short line across. Write f on our page.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib lowered the bag onto the dry path before adjusting its strap. One edge had folded over near the soft pad. He smoothed the fold instead of tugging at it.

speaker: narrator
text: Lark watched the strap settle flat. The bag still had room for every invitation. A tiny word on the journal’s checking strip ended with t. Nib studied it carefully.

speaker: nib
text: Our last sound matters, too,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib remembered proudly.

speaker: lark
text: It does,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark agreed warmly.

speaker: lark
text: Read the whole little word. Find fit.

speaker: narrator
text: The strap fitted comfortably again. Lark rested while Nib drew a very small story on the spare half of the page. His drawings showed two little mice called Sam and Pip, and a hand fan.

speaker: nib
text: A story about a fan,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib announced contentedly.

speaker: nib
text: A fan that has no opinions about directions.

speaker: narrator
text: Lark showed you the names before the reading. Capital S made the same sound as little s. Capital P made the same sound as little p. You already knew every sound in the words below.

speaker: lark
text: You can read this part yourself,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark invited gently.

speaker: lark
text: Take each sentence in turn. Let your finger follow underneath, and tap a word if you want help.

speaker: narrator
text: The little story had running, resting, and a helpful fan. Nib looked at his picture again. This time the picture could wait. The words told who had done each job.

speaker: lark
text: Who used the fan in our little story?

speaker: narrator
text: Lark asked gently.

speaker: lark
text: You can look back at the sentences.

speaker: narrator
text: Lark tucked the finished fork page into the route book. No new map section appeared. You had something more useful for today: the right path, a comfortable strap, and a clear record of the way you came.

speaker: narrator
text: The ferns thinned. Ahead, the creek flashed between pale stones. The path ended on a broad dry bank. A little clay pot stood on a low stump, and a reed-roofed hut waited across the water.

speaker: lark
text: Our first stop is getting nearer,

speaker: narrator
text: Lark murmured eagerly.

speaker: narrator
text: Nib counted the bag’s pockets with one careful paw. Three invitations. All safe. None delivered yet.

speaker: nib
text: First fork found,

speaker: narrator
text: Nib declared proudly.

speaker: nib
text: First delivery still to come.

speaker: narrator
text: A breeze stirred the reeds. Behind you, the wooden fan kept turning beside its own path. Ahead, the quiet little pot held the next clue.
